titulo: Health: the doctor and the pharmacy: The body and symptoms

aula.titulo: Health: the doctor and the pharmacy
aula.objetivo: Name parts of the body and common symptoms, say what hurts with «fare male» and «avere», talk to a doctor and a pharmacist with the polite «Lei» and the formal imperative, and use «da» for how long a symptom has lasted. Avoid the English-speaker traps: a possessive with body parts, «per» for something that is still going on, and «tu» forms with a doctor.

blocos.titulo: The body and symptoms: articles, «avere» and «fare male»
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: learn the parts of the body with their article: «la testa», «la gola», «la schiena», «lo stomaco». STEP 2: feminine nouns take «la». Masculine nouns that begin with «s» + consonant take «lo»: «lo stomaco», not «il stomaco». Other masculine nouns take «il»: «il raffreddore», «il mal di testa». STEP 3: to say what you have, use «avere»: «Ho la febbre» (I have a fever), «Ho la tosse», «Ho il raffreddore». STEP 4: pain with «mal di» + part of the body: «il mal di testa» (a headache), «Ho mal di gola» (I have a sore throat). After «avere» the phrase «mal di» usually has no article. STEP 5: the second way to talk about pain is «fare male» (to hurt): «Mi fa male la testa» (my head hurts). The verb agrees with the thing that hurts: «Mi fa male la testa» (one thing), but «Mi fanno male i piedi» (the feet, plural). STEP 6: with body parts Italian uses the definite article, not a possessive: «la testa», because «mi» already tells you whose head it is.
blocos.comparacao: English says «my head hurts» and «I have a headache», and it uses the possessive «my» with body parts. Italian leaves the possessive out: «Mi fa male la testa» is literally «to me hurts the head». English speakers often add the possessive anyway and say «Mi fa male la mia testa», which sounds wrong. English also has no grammatical gender, so each noun has to be learned with its article, and «lo» before «s» + consonant is new: «lo stomaco».

il raffreddore · il mal di testa
ho la febbre · ho la tosse · ho mal di gola

erros.motivo: «Stomaco» begins with «s» + consonant, so the masculine article is «lo», not «il».

erros.errado: Mi fa male la mia testa
erros.motivo: Body parts take the definite article. «Mi» already says whose head hurts, so there is no possessive.

itens.explicacao: Masculine nouns that begin with «s» + consonant take «lo».

itens.enunciado: How do you say «My head hurts»?
opcoes: Mi fa male la mia testa
itens.explicacao: The verb agrees with «la testa» (singular) and there is no possessive.

itens.enunciado: Which phrase means «I have a sore throat»?
itens.explicacao: «Avere» + «mal di» + the part of the body.

itens.enunciado: Put in order: «Mi fa male la testa»
itens.explicacao: «Mi fa male» and then the thing that hurts.

blocos.enunciado: Say six sentences aloud about what hurts or what you have, with «mi fa male», «ho mal di» and «ho la».
Say aloud the three articles of the lesson with one noun each: «la testa», «lo stomaco», «il raffreddore».
